reading: Segmentation is not the bottleneck; scan visibility and the volume step are. On the 76 items / 59 scans that have lift labels, foodscan's median item APE is 86% with GT labels and 86% with lift labels (segmentation adds almost nothing); per-dish totals 95% vs 95%. The noise-free GT surface (gt_top, oracle container pose) still gives 15% median / +10% bias on the same items.

Refined predictions (ptv3_short, only 3 scans / 4 paired items; no results/seg3d/v2_*/preds exist, only this run dumped predictions): foodscan median APE 34% with GT labels on the same voxel subset vs 33% with the predictions (dish 19% vs 20%); far too few scans to rank segmentation sources.

With GT labels (ok scans, n=285): median APE / median bias foodscan 76% / -71%, voxel 76% / -58%, hull 71% / -4% (mean APE 177%: the hull blows up on non-convex items), flat-table 77% / -26%. 61% of items are missing (<20 points) and 0% non-positive.

Where it fails 1, occlusion: items hidden >= 70% in the scan (n=237) come out -90% (median bias) with GT labels, yet the same items from the full GT surface give 50% APE: the integral is fine, the visible-only cloud has no height to integrate (column fill sums observed cells only, no completion).

Where it fails 2, stacking and voids: even from noise-free surfaces the container-relative column fill over-counts, +52% median bias in stacked scans (n=208) vs +33% in unstacked ones (n=88); an item sitting on another is charged for the item below, and loose piles / leaves / toppings are charged for their air gaps (gt_top median bias by kind: topping +725%, leaves +1471%, pile +70%, piece +4%).

By size (GT labels, foodscan): <10 mL median APE 55% (bias -26%), 10-50 mL 75%, >50 mL 87% (bias -87%): large items are the ones under-seen, small ones carry the 2 mm cell footprint bias (tests: +13% on a 1 cm cylinder, +4% on 3 cm) and the hull's +52% bias.

Registration: template ICP lands 1.5 mm median from the true pose but fails (>= 10 mm) on the sparse scans (94 of 285 ok items; run_meal's init is the centroid of all off-plane points, no multi-start, no fitness gate). Replacing ICP by the true pose changes the median APE only 76% -> 77%, so for these scans occlusion, not registration, is what hurts.

run_meal's item_volume crops the whole mesh by the item's bounding box, not by label; emulated on points (foodscan_bbox) the median APE goes 76% -> 81% (bias -71% -> -61%) because neighbours, cutlery and other items inside the box are integrated too.

Dish totals (what Nutrition5k-style scoring sees), foodscan: volume median APE 93% (bias -93%, n=71 dishes) with GT labels, 95% vs 95% GT vs lift labels on the 59 lift scans; under-seeing and over-counting partly cancel in the sum, so dish error is lower than item error. Mass with oracle density, 63 dishes with complete mass labels (volume APE 94% on them): 95% with the oracle category-median density, 94% with the oracle per-item density. Densities here are oracle, never predicted; mass_g is integer-rounded for small items.

Fix first: (1) get the hidden volume (shape completion / footprint-and-height prior per item, or more views) because visible-only height maps lose 90%+ on occluded items; (2) make stacked and loose items volume-consistent (subtract the supporting item's top, solid-fill factor for piles; compute dish totals as one union column map to avoid double counting); (3) crop by label instead of bbox in run_meal.item_volume; (4) give ContainerTemplate.register a container-label init and a fitness gate so failed registrations are flagged instead of silently used.
